name: Mars 3
note: First landing on Mars; it transmitted for about 20 seconds. Approximate position only

name: Viking 1
note: Chryse Planitia; worked until November 1982. Position from radio tracking (Folkner et al. 1997)

name: Viking 2
note: Utopia Planitia; contact ended in April 1980. Position from radio tracking (Folkner et al. 1997)

name: Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner
note: Ares Vallis; Sojourner was the first rover on Mars. Position from radio tracking (Folkner et al. 1997)

name: Beagle 2
note: Isidis Planitia; found partly deployed in HiRISE images in 2015

name: Spirit
note: Gusev Crater; drove 7.7 km and ended in 2010. Cartographic triangulation (Arvidson et al. 2004)

name: Opportunity
note: Meridiani Planum; drove 45.16 km and was last heard in June 2018. Cartographic triangulation (Arvidson et al. 2004)

name: Phoenix
note: Vastitas Borealis; found ice under the soil and saw snow fall from clouds (Smith et al. 2009)

name: Curiosity
note: Bradbury Landing in Gale Crater; still driving. First MMGIS waypoint (sol 3)

name: InSight
note: Elysium Planitia; recorded 1319 marsquakes. Planetocentric east in the IAU 2000 frame

name: Perseverance and Ingenuity
note: Octavia E. Butler Landing in Jezero Crater; still driving. First MMGIS waypoint (sol 13)

name: Zhurong (Tianwen-1)
note: Southern Utopia Planitia; drove about 2 km and has been silent since May 2022. Located in Tianwen-1 orbiter images
